Subject: Iterative model-improvement opt-out — DPA redlines

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and cost profile looked promising. Legal asked me to follow up on one DPA point before we sign: MediCorp needs an explicit, auditable opt-out that prevents our customer data from being used to improve or retrain models (both base-model updates and downstream fine-tuning) unless we provide affirmative consent.

I've attached a short proposed clause that our counsel prefers (iterative_opt_out_clause.txt) and a marked-up DPA (MediCorp_DPA_v2_redlines.docx). Key asks from their side:
- Clear definition of "Training" and "Model Improvement" that excludes derivative outputs used for serving (i.e., redaction/embedding indices allowed, training prohibited).
- A process for customers to request removal of their data from any training corpus within a reasonable window.
- A complete subprocessor list and 30 days notice for new subprocessors.

Can you confirm if Redwood can accept this carve-out as-is, or would you need a limited exception (e.g., aggregated/anonymous telemetry)? Also, what's the standard timeline for Docusign execution on your side?

Thanks,
Mei Lin\Head of Partnerships\SaaSCorp

Attachments: MediCorp_DPA_v2_redlines.docx, iterative_opt_out_clause.txt

Folks — forwarding inbound from MediCorp (Mei + Oliver). Asking for legal + sales guidance: can we accept an explicit universal opt-out for "training/model improvement"? Mei's attached clause is fairly categorical. Two immediate questions:

1) From a product/runtime perspective — is there a meaningful way to promise non-use for training while still providing features like embeddings, caching, or telemetry for reliability? (i.e., define "training" narrowly).
2) From legal/ops — they want a full subprocessor list and 30 days' notice. We can provide the list but need to confirm notice cadence and whether 30 days is acceptable.

Suggested next steps: Neha, can you propose redlines back to their doc and suggest compromise language (e.g., allow anonymized/aggregate usage for service improvement but no training of models that include customer data tied to accounts). Marissa, loop in CS if we need to offer product-level mitigations (dedicated/private deployments / disabled telemetry).

I'll hold on sending anything to DocuSign until we agree. HubSpot: DEAL-4578.

Thanks — Jonas\Account Executive\Redwood Inference

Jonas / Marissa — thanks for the ping. Quick read and recommendations below (high level):

High-level risk: MediCorp's clause, as drafted, is a full prohibition on using any Customer Data for "training" or "model improvement". That's aggressive and will block downstream uses we frequently rely on for quality patches and safety. We can accept an opt-out with careful scoping. Proposed trade: keep the customer's right to opt-out, but narrow definitions and add operational controls.

Proposed redlines (summary):
- Define terms:
  * "Customer Data": data submitted by or on behalf of the customer through the API or via integrations.
  * "Training/Model Improvement": any process that incorporates Customer Data into a persistent model weight update or fine-tuning dataset intended to change model behavior.
  * Exclude: metrics, telemetry, aggregated/anonymous usage data and transient cache data used solely for serving and latency improvements.
- Carve-out: Allow use of fully de-identified, aggregated datasets that cannot be reconstructed to identify customer accounts.
- Removal process: Acceptable: provide an account-level opt-out request; Redwood will (1) stop including new data in training pipelines within 30 days and (2) use commercially reasonable efforts to remove previously ingested data from future training iterations within 180 days, subject to technical limitations.
- Subprocessors: provide current full list; 30 days notice for new subprocessors is ok if we pair with a standard "emergency" exception for security incidents (with immediate notice).

I can produce a tracked-changes draft to send back to MediCorp. Also, product needs to confirm what "stop including new data" means: we should be explicit about logs, KV cache TTLs, and whether embeddings derived from user data are considered Customer Data for the opt-out.

I'll draft language and attach a redline: MediCorp_DPA_v2_redlines_neha_v1.docx.

—Neha\Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance\Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: subprocessor_list_2027-05.csv

Subject: Re: Iterative model-improvement opt-out — DPA redlines

Mei / Oliver — thanks for sending this over. Copied Neha (legal) who reviewed and proposed a compromise. Quick product clarifications to make the carve-out workable:

- "Training/Model Improvement" will be defined as you suggested: any process that ingests Customer Data into a persistent training dataset or fine-tunes model weights.
- What we consider acceptable:
  1) Telemetry/operational metrics (latency, error rates) — allowed as aggregated and anonymized for the purpose of service reliability.
  2) Embeddings / derived vectors used for serving (search/retrieval) — allowed for the customer's account only, but explicitly excluded from training pipelines when opt-out is active.
  3) Caching / KV stores used to accelerate inference — these are transient and not treated as training data, but we'll commit to TTLs and documentation on retention.

Neha suggests the following timelines if MediCorp opts out:
- Stop new inclusion in training: within 30 days of a documented opt-out request.
- Effort to remove prior data from future training: commercially reasonable efforts, target 180 days where technically feasible.

If that looks acceptable, Neha will send a tracked changes DPA and we can prepare the DocuSign envelope. For transparency, here's the HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4578.

Jonas\Account Executive\Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_list_2027-05.csv (current subprocessors)
